concept.name: Argo CD GitOps

relationships.description: Connects Argo CD GitOps to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Argo CD is a declarative, pull-based GitOps continuous delivery controller for Kubernetes that continuously reconciles live cluster state against Git repositories.
spark.keyTakeaway: Git is the single source of truth: Argo CD's in-cluster controller pulls desired manifests and self-heals configuration drift without exposing cluster credentials to external CI runners.

concept.whyItMatters: Push-based CI/CD pipelines (`kubectl apply` from GitHub Actions) require giving external CI runners cluster-admin credentials and leave clusters blind to manual `kubectl edit` drift. Argo CD runs inside Kubernetes, detects `OutOfSync` drift within seconds (or via webhooks), and reconciles Helm, Kustomize, or plain YAML deterministically with instant Git-revert rollbacks.
whenToUse: Managing multi-environment (dev/staging/prod) or multi-cluster Kubernetes deployments where auditability and drift detection are mandatory.
Eliminating external CI/CD access to production Kubernetes API servers in regulated or zero-trust environments.
Orchestrating progressive delivery (canary/blue-green) alongside Argo Rollouts or fleet-wide add-ons via `ApplicationSet` generators.
whenNotToUse: Non-Kubernetes infrastructure provisioning (VPCs, IAM roles, RDS instances), where Terraform/OpenTofu or Crossplane is the right control plane.
Ephemeral PR preview environments that need imperatively scripted teardown hooks faster than Git commit/PR lifecycle workflows.
Single-node hobby clusters where a 10-line CI deploy script is simpler than operating Argo CD's repo-server, Redis, and controller.
keyPoints: Pull-based reconciliation loop: Argo CD's `application-controller` compares the live Kubernetes API state against the rendered Git target state every 3 minutes (default `timeout.reconciliation`) or immediately on Git webhook.
Three-component architecture: `argocd-server` (API/UI/RBAC), `argocd-repo-server` (clones Git and renders Helm/Kustomize/Jsonnet), and `argocd-application-controller` (diffs and applies).
Sync vs. Health are independent: `Synced` means live manifests match Git; `Healthy` means Pods/Deployments pass readiness checks—an app can be `Synced` yet `Degraded`.
Sync waves and hooks (`PreSync`, `Sync`, `PostSync`) order dependencies—such as running a DB migration Job in wave `-1` before rolling out Deployments in wave `0`.
App-of-Apps and `ApplicationSet`: `ApplicationSet` replaces brittle nested App-of-Apps patterns using Git directory, list, or cluster generators to template 100s of apps cleanly.

examples.title: Fleet-Wide Add-On Management with ApplicationSets
examples.scenario: A platform team manages Prometheus, ExternalDNS, and Kyverno across 35 EKS clusters.
examples.outcome: A single `ApplicationSet` using a `clusters` generator renders per-cluster Helm values from Git, rolling out updates in controlled waves with zero manual `kubectl` context switching.

examples.title: Automatic Drift Self-Healing in Production
examples.scenario: An on-call engineer runs `kubectl scale deploy/checkout --replicas=10` during an incident, forgetting to update Git.
examples.outcome: With `selfHeal: true`, Argo CD detects the replica count mismatch against Git's `replicas: 4` within 3 minutes and either reverts it (enforcing GitOps) or highlights `OutOfSync` if auto-heal is intentionally paused.

tradeOffs.pro: Zero-touch continuous delivery; manual `kubectl` hotfixes are automatically reverted to preserve compliance.
tradeOffs.con: Urgent incident mitigations must go through Git (or temporarily disable auto-sync), adding 1–2 minutes if CI checks block merges.

tradeOffs.pro: Separating `app-repo` (CI builds image) from `gitops-config-repo` (Argo CD watches) prevents infinite CI-trigger loops.
tradeOffs.con: Requires CI or Argo CD Image Updater to open automated PRs/commits to bump image tags across repos.

tradeOffs.factor: Plain Secrets vs. External Secrets Operator (ESO)
tradeOffs.pro: Committing encrypted SealedSecrets/SOPS keeps everything self-contained in Git.
tradeOffs.con: ESO/Vault integration avoids storing any secret material—even encrypted—in Git history and simplifies key rotation.

failureModes.name: Helm/Kustomize Rendering Timeout in `repo-server`
failureModes.description: Large monorepos or slow `helm dependency build` calls exhaust `argocd-repo-server` CPU/memory, stalling all app syncs with `ComparisonError`.
failureModes.mitigation: Pin Helm chart versions in an internal OCI registry, scale `repo-server` replicas, and set `ARGOCD_EXEC_TIMEOUT` appropriately.

failureModes.name: Endless Sync Loop on Mutated Fields
failureModes.description: A mutating webhook (e.g., Istio sidecar injector or HPA changing `spec.replicas`) alters live resources, causing Argo CD to report perpetual `OutOfSync` and re-apply.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure `ignoreDifferences` (e.g., `/spec/replicas` when HPA is active) or use Server-Side Apply (`ServerSideApply=true`).

failureModes.name: Accidental `Prune=true` Mass Deletion
failureModes.description: A bad refactor renames a Kustomize path or deletes an `Application` with `cascade=true` and `prune: true`, wiping production Deployments and PVCs.
failureModes.mitigation: Add `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false` on stateful PVCs/Namespaces and require PR review on `ApplicationSet` changes.

failureModes.name: Kubernetes API Rate Limiting (429)
failureModes.description: Managing 500+ Applications from one controller without sharding overwhelms the kube-apiserver with list/watch and patch calls.
failureModes.mitigation: Enable controller sharding (`--sharding-method=round-robin`), increase `--kube-api-qps`, and use Git webhooks instead of polling every 30s.

commonMistakes: Pointing Argo CD at the same repository where CI runs without `[skip ci]` or a separate config repo, causing infinite commit loops.
Leaving `spec.replicas` hardcoded in Git Deployments alongside a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA), triggering constant scale fights.
Committing unencrypted Kubernetes `Secret` manifests to Git instead of using External Secrets Operator, SealedSecrets, or SOPS.
Using `latest` image tags in Git manifests—Argo CD cannot detect a new digest behind `latest`, breaking rollbacks and reproducibility.
Enabling `selfHeal: true` and `prune: true` globally on production databases without `Prune=false` annotations on PersistentVolumeClaims.

sections.content:
## The idea

Argo CD turns Kubernetes deployments inside out: instead of an external CI pipeline pushing `kubectl apply` with long-lived admin tokens, an in-cluster controller continuously **pulls** desired state from Git and reconciles it against the live Kubernetes API. Every change—image bumps, RBAC rules, Helm values—is a Git commit, giving you cryptographic audit trails, `git revert` rollbacks, and automatic drift detection.

## Concrete walkthrough

Suppose CI builds `ghcr.io/acme/billing:v1.4.2` and updates `envs/prod/billing/kustomization.yaml` in the `platform-gitops` repo.

1. **Webhook & Fetch**: GitHub sends a webhook to `argocd-server`, which notifies `argocd-application-controller` to bypass the 3-minute polling interval.
2. **Render**: `argocd-repo-server` clones `platform-gitops` at the new commit SHA, runs `kustomize build envs/prod/billing`, and caches the rendered YAML in Redis.
3. **Diff**: The controller compares the rendered target manifests against the live `billing` namespace state in Kubernetes, flagging the Deployment as `OutOfSync`.
4. **Wave-Ordered Sync**: The controller executes a `PreSync` schema-migration Job (wave `-1`), waits for `Complete`, then applies the Deployment (wave `0`) using Server-Side Apply and monitors readiness until Health returns `Healthy`.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Sync phases, waves, and Server-Side Apply
sections.content:
## Sync phases, waves, and Server-Side Apply

Real deployments require ordering. Argo CD executes syncs in three phases: `PreSync` (e.g., DB schema migrations), `Sync` (main workloads), and `PostSync` (smoke tests, Slack notifications). Within each phase, `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` integers (default `0`, ascending order) ensure CRDs and Namespaces land before Custom Resources.

Enabling `ServerSideApply=true` in `syncOptions` delegates field ownership and strategic merges to the Kubernetes API server, eliminating the 262 KB `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation limit on large CRDs (like Prometheus Operator or Istio).

## GitOps deployment patterns compared

| Pattern | Best For | Pros | Watch-Outs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Single `Application`** | Standalone service or small team | Simple YAML; easy RBAC scoping | Manual boilerplate per cluster/env |
| **App-of-Apps** | Legacy hierarchical grouping | Pure `Application` CRDs | Cascading delete risk; harder templating |
| **`ApplicationSet` (Matrix/Git)** | Multi-cluster & multi-tenant fleets | Dynamic generation from Git dirs or cluster labels | Bad generator edit affects all child apps |
| **Argo Rollouts + GitOps** | Canary & blue-green prod releases | Automated Prometheus/Datadog metric analysis | Requires ingress/mesh traffic-split integration |

## Failure modes

1. **HPA vs. Git Replica Fight**: Leaving `replicas: 3` in Git when HPA scales pods to 8 causes Argo CD `selfHeal` to scale pods back down to 3. Fix: omit `replicas` from Git or add `/spec/replicas` to `ignoreDifferences`.
2. **Orphaned Finalizer Deadlock**: Deleting an `Application` with `resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io` hangs forever if the target cluster is unreachable. Fix: patch out the finalizer only after verifying the target cluster is decommissioned.
3. **CRD Annotation Overflow**: Applying large CRDs with client-side apply fails with `metadata.annotations: Too long`. Fix: use `ServerSideApply=true` and `Replace=true` for CRDs.
4. **Shared `repo-server` Bottleneck**: One overloaded `repo-server` pod running slow Helm plugins delays syncs for the entire org. Fix: scale `repo-server` horizontally and enable Redis caching.

## Scaling Argo CD across teams

Separate your Argo CD control plane from application workloads on a dedicated management cluster, and isolate teams with `AppProject` boundaries (`sourceRepos`, `destinations`, `clusterResourceWhitelist`) mapped to OIDC groups. Pair Argo CD with External Secrets Operator (ESO) so Git holds only `ExternalSecret` pointers to AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault, never raw credentials.

## Practical checklist

- **Pin immutable tags or digests**: never reference `:latest` in GitOps manifests; use semantic tags + SHA256 digests.
- **Protect stateful resources**: set `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false` on PVCs, Namespaces, and DBs.
- **Enable Server-Side Apply**: add `ServerSideApply=true` to avoid CRD annotation size limits and field-manager conflicts.
- **Configure `ignoreDifferences`**: whitelist HPA-managed `/spec/replicas` and webhook-injected fields.
- **Use separate config repos**: decouple CI build repos from GitOps manifest repos and wire Git webhooks for sub-second sync triggers.

interviewProblems.title: Argo CD GitOps
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Argo CD GitOps. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Argo CD is a declarative, pull-based GitOps continuous delivery controller for Kubernetes that continuously reconciles live cluster state against Git repositories.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Application Controller applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Target K8s Cluster.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Target K8s Cluster experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Pin Helm chart versions in an internal OCI registry, scale `repo-server` replicas, and set `ARGOCD_EXEC_TIMEOUT` appropriately.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Git is the single source of truth: Argo CD's in-cluster controller pulls desired manifests and self-heals configuration drift without exposing cluster credentials to external CI runners.
Avoid trap: Pointing Argo CD at the same repository where CI runs without `[skip ci]` or a separate config repo, causing infinite commit loops.
Avoid trap: Leaving `spec.replicas` hardcoded in Git Deployments alongside a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA), triggering constant scale fights.
When to reach for it: Managing multi-environment (dev/staging/prod) or multi-cluster Kubernetes deployments where auditability and drift detection are mandatory.
When to reach for it: Eliminating external CI/CD access to production Kubernetes API servers in regulated or zero-trust environments.

putItTogether.title: Putting Argocd Gitops Together
putItTogether.summary: Git is the single source of truth: Argo CD's in-cluster controller pulls desired manifests and self-heals configuration drift without exposing cluster credentials to external CI runners.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Argocd Gitops before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: A single `ApplicationSet` using a `clusters` generator renders per-cluster Helm values from Git, rolling out updates in controlled waves with zero manual `kubectl` context switching.
